analyst_view.overall: Early view: Game 2 at Providence Park on Saturday 28 November (7:30 pm PT), a week after Game 1 in Frisco; a draw goes to penalties. Portland drew 2-2 with Dallas here in the regular season and won four in a row to finish under Marti Cifuentes, while Dallas scored a club-record 62 goals. If Dallas win Game 1, Portland must win to force a decider, which should open the game up.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals and I lean slightly higher. The league meeting here finished 2-2, Portland conceded 61 goals in the season even while scoring freely, and Dallas have Musa, Valiente and Kaick after scoring three against Colorado.

corners.text: The site expects 10.3 corners, more for Portland at home. I found nothing on either team's wide play or set pieces that moves this, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. There is playoff history between these clubs (three series since 2015), but I found no recent discipline news or referee information, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The site expects 25.7 shots. Portland have been creating a lot during their winning run (they out-created Charlotte by a wide margin in October) and Dallas attack well, so I lean a little higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 on target. I lean slightly higher with the goals: both defences have conceded plenty and both attacks have scorers in form, Ariel Lassiter and Kristoffer Velde for Portland and Kaick for Dallas.
